description: The innermost and smallest of Uranus's five major moons — and visually the most extreme. Voyager 2's flyby imagery revealed a surface that looks like it was assembled from mismatched pieces: enormous cliffs, fractured plateaus, and concentric coronae jutting from heavily-cratered older terrain. The leading hypothesis is that Miranda was disrupted by an impact at least once, with the fragments reassembling under their own gravity. Verona Rupes drops ~20 km — under Miranda's low gravity, a falling object would take roughly 12 minutes to reach the bottom.
surface_composition: Water-ice + silicate rock; surface a patchwork of ancient cratered terrain crossed by huge coronae — concentric ridges and grooves that include Verona Rupes, the tallest known cliff in the solar system (~20 km vertical drop).
mission_visits: Voyager 2 — USA, 1986 (only spacecraft visit; southern-hemisphere flyby)

science_sections.why: Miranda has the highest orbital inclination (4.3°) of the major Uranian moons — combined with an early-system disruption event, it explains the famous cliff faces Voyager 2 imaged in 1986.
